response.markdown_report:
**Recommendation: validate the existing NextItNet diagnostic adapter with bounded, reversible faults before adding further probes.** At 20% progress, this offers a feasible foundation for subsequent training experiments.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Sampled training pairwise accuracy is 96.64–99.33%. This establishes fitted-pair separation, while held-out HR@10 remains unavailable. (2) Endpoint effective ranks span 18.21–29.22. These describe representation variation without demonstrating relevance or temporal reasoning. (3) Local-signal measurements are unavailable, and candidate-depth reports identify their category as unknown. Explicit interface checks should precede stronger interpretations.

**Insights from related work.** (1) NextItNet’s causal convolutions determine possible temporal influence [1]. Measured influence still requires behavioral checks. (2) Recommender metamorphic testing examines expected relationships between outputs [2]. Mutation testing can assess whether those checks detect deliberately introduced faults [3]. (3) Activation-patching results depend on corruption, location and metric [4]. Restoration and sham controls are therefore necessary when adapting patching to recommendation.

The research directions are interface integrity, diagnostic sensitivity, and temporal dependence. Their conceptual map is:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Gap | Proposed measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interface integrity | Identity/batch checks pass | Routing and readout coverage | Explicit category and readout controls |
| Diagnostic sensitivity | Numerous descriptive probes | Unknown fault detection | Reversible mutation panel |
| Temporal dependence | Perturbation machinery | Omitted paired outcomes | Fixed-candidate rank contrasts |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Explicit category/scorer contract | 2/6/2 | Makes unsupported analyses explicit | Primarily integration work |
| **Reversible fault calibration** [2,3] | **4/7/4** | Tests diagnostic sensitivity without retraining | Synthetic faults may poorly represent natural failures |
| Paired block restoration [1,4] | 5/7/6 | Localizes dependence within one network | Corruption choices complicate interpretation |

The selected algorithm freezes a small training-prefix panel and its candidate IDs. It records clean outputs, then temporarily introduces incorrect count-minus-one readout, controlled future dependence, or residual-branch suppression. Positive score scaling supplies a ranking-invariance control. Each intervention has a predefined expected response; restoration must reproduce clean outputs within tolerance.

Report readout disagreement, future-feature sensitivity, ranking invariance, restoration error, and conditional fault-detection counts. A suppressed branch without measurable output change is behaviorally inactive on this panel, rather than a detected fault. All target ranks remain in-sample diagnostics.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, `run_full_diagnosis`, the interpretation-prompt function, and every ModelView interface. Apply interventions only within the diagnostic harness and restore state in `finally`. Retain one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category. Subsequent training changes require the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; this audit claims no ranking improvement.

idea.description: Calibrate the existing NextItNet diagnostic adapter using a small panel of reversible faults and invariance controls on fixed training examples, without fitting another model or changing production inference.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics show strong sampled training separation, but several measurements are unavailable or incompletely attributed. Before using additional diagnostics to motivate training changes, establish which checks detect concrete interface and temporal faults and which merely summarize scores.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch and all ModelView interfaces. view.model remains the actual trained NextItNet nn.Module. Require explicit category identity for named category reports; unknown identity produces an unavailable macro aggregation rather than an inferred route. Unsupported scorer or objective contracts remain null with reasons.

Use up to 32 deterministically selected identified training users per category, local seed 42, and fixed training-prefix targets and candidate IDs. Require nonempty prefixes; include left-padded histories with varying lengths. Use only permitted training histories and available metadata. Preserve baseline candidate eligibility and document repeated targets. Training-prefix target ranks are in-sample diagnostic outcomes, never validation estimates.

For clean features, gather the largest nonzero sequence index. Implement the incorrect count-minus-one gather only as a temporary diagnostic mutation. Report how many examples have different indices and how many exhibit measurable feature or score differences. Distinguish mutation activation from probe detection.

Use future-token perturbations to check earlier causal features. For a positive-control mutation, temporarily add a small, declared future-embedding contribution to an earlier valid feature at a supported diagnostic boundary. Document that this tests the causal-check machinery at that boundary, not every encoder pathway. Run residual-branch suppression only when the graph is recognized and safely hookable; otherwise return null with a reason. Output changes from suppression have no universal desirable direction.

Apply positive score scaling as a control: ordinal rankings should remain invariant apart from documented numerical or tie-handling issues, while raw margins may change. Reuse the baseline tie rule. Predeclare tolerances and fault severities before observing results. Report activated, behaviorally effective, detected and unavailable cases separately. Detection rates are conditional on this synthetic panel; avoid population specificity claims from a small set of controls.

Save each module's mode, global RNG states and pre-existing hooks; use no_grad and local generators. Remove temporary hooks and restore modes and RNG states in finally, then verify clean-output restoration. Do not alter weights, optimizer state, checkpoints, scoring routes or production predictor behavior. Record synchronized runtime and trial-local artifacts. Keep the suite bounded because diagnostics consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the supplied splits and evaluator. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. No fusion, auxiliary fitted predictor, hidden-test access or additional data is introduced.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    retain existing bounded measurements and definitions
    save module modes and global RNG states
    temporary_handles = []
    try:
        set actual NextItNet model to eval mode
        panel = select_fixed_training_prefix_panel(local_seed=42, cap=32)
        freeze candidate IDs, exclusions, tie rule and category identity
        clean = evaluate(panel, readout=largest_nonzero_index)
        controls = rerun_clean_and_positive_score_scaling(panel)
        for mutation in predefined_supported_mutations:
            determine applicable examples and expected probe response
            install temporary mutation within diagnostic execution
            mutated = evaluate_same_panel()
            measure activation, behavioral effect and expected detection
            remove mutation immediately
            restored = evaluate_same_panel()
            check restored outputs against clean within declared tolerance
        report counts, paired differences, control violations and runtime
        mark unsupported probes null with reasons
    finally:
        remove all remaining temporary handles
        restore module modes and global RNG states
    return {'metrics': measured_results,
            'metric_definitions': populations_expected_relations_and_limitations}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measurements, definitions, applicability and missingness
    distinguish synthetic fault detection from natural model failures
    distinguish in-sample ranks from pinned validation HR@10
    prohibit unsupported intent, compatibility and performance claims

originality.positive: Combines reversible NextItNet-specific readout and causality faults with paired candidate measurements and restoration checks.
originality.negative: The underlying metamorphic and mutation-testing principles are established; this is a targeted adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable way to assess whether increasingly elaborate recommendation diagnostics respond to known faults before spending budget on training interventions.
future_potential.negative: Synthetic fault sensitivity does not demonstrate sensitivity to natural recommendation failures or predict validation gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no retraining, additional checkpoint or production architecture change, and uses a small fixed panel.
code_difficulty.negative: Safe temporary hooks, mutation applicability, numerical controls and complete state restoration require careful integration.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for family-specific temporal and branch probes.
limitations: Architectural reachability alone does not show which history positions a fitted model uses.

related_work.title: Recommender metamorphic-testing study (2024; supplied reference)
contributions: Studies expected output relationships as reliability checks for recommender implementations.
limitations: The supplied summary concerns other recommender frameworks and does not validate these NextItNet-specific relations.

related_work.title: Recommender mutation-testing study (2025; supplied reference)
contributions: Assesses relation effectiveness and sensitivity using deliberate mutations and varied inputs.
limitations: Detection of synthetic mutations does not establish detection of naturally occurring recommendation errors.

related_work.title: Activation-patching interpretation guidance (2024; supplied reference)
contributions: Provides methodological guidance for interpreting activation interventions and their dependence on experimental choices.
limitations: Does not provide a validated NextItNet-specific patching protocol or establish causal user intent.
